label: sparse: <DEL>/first copy steps in long sequences starting with o/f/g/i/p (weak)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). Activation is concentrated at the delimiter step (35% of mass, 4.3x lift) and the first 1-2 copy steps, with higher rates for long sequences (L=9 holds 52% of mass) and when the token being recalled or the input is o, f, g, p, q or i (sequences that start with o/f/g/i, often with q early on). It never fires at t=0 or 1, and the remaining activations are spread over original-phase steps 2-3 and late copy steps. No simple predicate isolates it: every candidate tried has precision of 2% or less (best dev F1 about 0.04), because the feature fires on only a small, unpredictable fraction of the steps each candidate selects. The recorded predicate covers about 26% of activation mass. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.23), and the strongest activations land on <DEL> or the first copied token.
